blocks.text: After deploying a Zero Trust Branch appliance or virtual machine (VM), you need to configure the VLAN that must be protected in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Ensure that a LAN port on the Zero Trust Branch appliance is connected to the switch, and the switch port must be configured as a trunk port with the relevant VLAN IDs permitted. This ensures the appliance is in the same VLAN as the devices (broadcast packets from the devices must reach the LAN port).

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Branch > Deployments > Sites.
On the Sites page, search for and click the site name for which the VLAN must be added.
See image.
On the site details page, click the VLANs tab, and click Add VLAN.
See image.
In the Add VLAN drawer:
VLAN Name: Enter a name for the VLAN.
VLAN ID: Enter an ID for the VLAN.
Zone: Select a zone from the drop-down menu:
LAN Zone: Select this if the VLAN is configured on the LAN-side interface with endpoints.
Management Zone: Select this if the VLAN is configured on the management-side interface.
WAN Zone: Select this if the VLAN is configured on the WAN-side interface.
See image.

IGMP Settings: Select Enable IGMP Querier and select the appropriate version (IGMPv2 or IGMPv3) supported in your environment from the IGMP Version drop-down menu. Enabling IGMP querier allows the Zero Trust Branch appliance to send periodical IGMP Query messages and maintain multicast group membership within the VLAN.
IGMP querier is supported only on Zero Trust Branch appliances running version 8.1.2 or later.
See image.
Configure interfaces and network settings based on the zone selected:
LAN-side interface and network settings
In the Interfaces section, select the interface from the Interface for Appliance drop-down menu.
In the Network section:
Interface IP: Enter the IP address of the interface.
DHCP Profile: Select a DHCP profile from the drop-down menu.
Per-VLAN DCHP profiles are supported only on Zero Trust Branch appliances running version 8.1.2 or later.
See image.
In the Segmentation section:
Use DHCP: Enable this option to assign IP addresses to devices using DHCP. Configure the following settings:
Granularity: Select one of the following options:
Device (/32): Assigns /32 subnet masks to endpoints, placing each device in a network of one. Select this option if you need full isolation for the devices in this VLAN.
Network: Assigns the original subnet mask to all endpoints connected to this VLAN.
DHCP Range: Enter the starting and ending IP addresses for the DHCP address range.
See image.
Use Micro-subnets: Enable this option to allocate an additional IP address range for statically configured devices in micro-subnets. Configure the following settings:
Micro-subnet Prefix: Select the subnet prefix (/30, /29, /28, or /27) to determine the size of each micro-subnet.
Micro-subnets Range: Enter the starting and ending IP addresses for the micro-subnets range.
See image.

If you have enabled the Use DHCP option (Device (/32) or Network), you can choose to use reserved IP addresses for specific assets. To learn more, see Understanding Protection Solutions and Configuring IP Address Reservation for Assets within a VLAN.
In the Options section:
Private DNS Servers: Enter the IP address of the private DNS servers that must be used for the VLAN and click Add. You can add multiple private DNS servers.
See image.
Management-side interface and network settings
In the Interfaces section:
Appliance: Select the appliance from the drop-down menu.
Interface for Appliance: Select one of the following management interfaces from the drop-down menu:
lo0 (Management): Uses the loopback interface for in-band management within the main routing domain.
ge3 (Management): Uses a dedicated physical interface for out-of-band management through a separate management VRF.
See image.
In the Network section:
For loopback interface (in-band management)
This configuration applies only if lo0 (Management) is selected as the Interface for Appliance option.
Interface IP: Enter the IP address of the interface.
See image.
For dedicated physical interface (out-of-band management)
This configuration applies only if ge3 (Management) is selected as the Interface for Appliance option.
Use DHCP for IP Address: Enable this option to obtain the IP address for the interface automatically through DHCP.
IP Address: Enter the IP address of the interface in CIDR notation. This option is shown only if Use DHCP for IP Address is disabled.
Default Gateway IP: Enter the IP address of the default gateway. This option is shown only if Use DHCP for IP Address is disabled.
See image.
A gateway must be configured on the management interface to allow access to Zero Trust Branch through the management interface from any network.
If the management interface is used to monitor appliances using SNMP over Private Access, only active appliances can be monitored.
WAN-side interface and network settings
In the Interfaces section:
Appliance: Select the appliance from the drop-down menu.
Interface for Appliance: Select the interface from the drop-down menu.
In the Network section:

Use DHCP for IP Address: Enable this option if you want to use DHCP addressing. Otherwise, disable this option, and enter the respective IP addresses for the Interface IP and Default Gateway IP fields.
Virtual IP: (Optional) Enter a virtual IP address if the upstream router requires a consistent return address for reverse routing.
See image.
Click Add.

Log in to your existing L2/L3 switch, router, or firewall, and shut down the SVI/VLAN interface. Add a return route for VLAN with the Zero Trust Branch WAN Virtual IP address as a nexthop. Here are sample commands from the switch or L3 device (for VLAN 226 with subnet mask 10.16.226.0/24):
#conf t #int vlan 226 #shutdown #exit #ip route 10.16.226.0 255.255.255.0 < airgap-wan-vip >
On the VLANs tab, click the toggle in the Enable column.
See image.
By default, the VLANs are created in the staged state. Each VLAN must be enabled to configure it into the branch appliances or VMs.

blocks.heading: Configuring a VLAN for DNS Proxy

blocks.text: You can specify a single VLAN to serve as the source IP address for outbound DNS requests made from the appliance's DNS proxy. This is needed when an upstream DNS server requires a fixed, internal source IP address, and when the server is accessed via a Routed Tunnel.
To configure a VLAN for DNS proxy:

blocks.item: Go to Zero Trust Branch > Deployments > Sites.
In the Site Name column, click the name of the site you want to configure.
Click the VLANs tab.
Click the Gear icon in the row for the desired VLAN, and then select Use for DNS Proxy.
A DNS Proxy tag appears in the Features column for the selected VLAN.
See image.

blocks.text: You can designate only one VLAN per site. Selecting a different VLAN will automatically clear the previous selection.
To configure a VLAN with an ebond interface, complete the following steps in the Zscaler Admin Console:

blocks.item: 1. Create or clone a template.
Templates are the prerequisites for adding a new site in Zero Trust Branch. For bonding interfaces, create a new custom template or clone a default template. To learn more, see Managing Templates.
2. Add a bonding interface.
From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Branch > Resources > Templates.
On the Templates page, click the required template name.
See image.
On the Template page, click the Interfaces tab, click Add, and then select Bonding Interface.
See image.
In the Add Bonding Interface drawer:
Name: Select the bonding interface name (ebond0 or ebond1) from the drop-down menu.
Appliance: Specify the Zero Trust Branch appliance associated with the bonding interface.
Interface Type: Select the type of physical interface (None, LAN, or WAN) included in the bonding interface.

Member Interfaces: Select the physical interfaces that must be members of the bonding interface. These interfaces are aggregated to form one virtual link with combined throughput and failover capabilities. Members must have the same port speed.
See image.
Click Add.
Bonding interfaces support tagging (with 802.1Q, sub-interfaces) for both LAN and WAN. After the bonding interface is created, it appears under the Interfaces tab for the template.
The template with the bonding interface is now available to add a site.
3. Add a VLAN.
After the Zero Trust Branch appliance is registered, you must add the VLANs as the switched virtual interface (SVI) moved to Zero Trust Branch. To learn more, see Configuring a VLAN.
The ebond interface is now available for use.
4. Configure the switch.

The following example shows how to configure a port channel on a Cisco 3560 switch. In this configuration, two physical FastEthernet interfaces, FastEthernet0/1 and FastEthernet0/4, are combined to form a single logical port channel, which connects to a ZT800. This setup uses the Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) for dynamic link aggregation.
The following is a sample for reference only. It is recommended to use the appropriate parameters based on the switch model and network environment you are working with.

interface Port-channel1 switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20 switchport mode trunk ! interface FastEthernet0/1 switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20 switchport mode trunk channel-group 1 mode active ! interface FastEthernet0/4 switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20 switchport mode trunk channel-group 1 mode active !
5. Verify the ebond status.
Verify the bonding interface status in the console.
See image.
Verify the Cisco 3560 physical and port-channel interfaces. The following is a sample. You can modify the verification as required.
